hero.headline: Oil Demand Takes Hit as Prices Spike from Iran Crisis
hero.body:
Major investment banks are reporting a significant drop in global oil demand as prices surge during the ongoing Iran crisis. Goldman Sachs has revised its demand forecasts downward, citing what economists call demand destruction, a sustained loss of consumption caused by high prices.

The nine-day conflict has caused a substantial spike in oil prices, with West Texas Intermediate crude rising 35 percent in a single week. This surge has rippled through fuel markets globally, with gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel all jumping sharply. In the United States, regular gasoline prices climbed 14 percent in one week to $3.41 per gallon.

Chris Wright, the US Department of Energy secretary, stated that elevated energy prices would persist for weeks rather than months. He predicted that domestic prices would ultimately fall back below $3 per gallon, adding that normalcy would return in the short term. Wright also noted that the US is not targeting Iran's energy infrastructure and expects shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to resume more regularly soon, though current traffic remains far below the typical 80 to 90 tankers per day.

Demand destruction occurs when commodity prices rise high enough that buyers permanently reduce consumption rather than temporarily cutting back. The spike in oil costs has forced businesses and consumers to cut back on fuel use, raising questions about whether the current crisis has accelerated a longer-term shift away from oil dependence.

The impact extends beyond fuel prices. Japan is experiencing shortages of plastic bags, trays, and food service gloves due to a naphtha shortage. Naphtha, extracted from crude oil in the Middle East, serves as a key ingredient for plastic production. The food sector, which accounts for nearly one-third of Japan's annual plastic consumption, has been hit particularly hard, with some outlets now offering incentives to customers who bring their own containers.

The United Nations has also sounded alarms about broader consequences. The World Food Programme warned that soaring oil prices are devastating global food security, with nearly three months into the conflict bringing the organization's pessimistic predictions closer to reality. Officials worry that extended conflict could push tens of millions of people into acute hunger.

The changes from this crisis could reshape the energy sector in ways that extend beyond the immediate situation. Industry observers are tracking whether businesses and consumers who have reduced oil consumption will return to previous usage levels once prices stabilize, or whether the shock will produce permanent shifts in energy demand. The outcome will depend partly on how long elevated prices persist and what alternatives become available during the adjustment period.

Financial analysts are warning that the oil industry faces significant demand shock, with implications for energy markets worldwide. Economists point to shifts in transportation habits, industrial production adjustments, and increased investment in alternative energy as typical responses to sustained price increases.

cards.headline: Trump administration delays major drone deal with Ukraine
cards.teaser: The White House has not signed an agreement with Ukraine on drone production despite months of talks and Ukrainian requests.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's hesitation to sign a major drone deal with Ukraine is slowing U.S. military progress in an area where it already lags. Talks between the two nations have stretched back to at least September, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urging Washington to finalize the agreement.

The delay is affecting the U.S. military's ability to advance its drone capabilities. The prolonged negotiations have left experts questioning why the administration has not moved forward on a deal that Ukrainian leadership considers important for both countries' defense capabilities.

cards.headline: China increases patrols near Taiwan after Japan-Philippines talks
cards.teaser: Beijing deployed coast guard and research ships near key South China Sea islands in protest.
cards.body:
China escalated naval patrols near Taiwan following talks between Japan and the Philippines. Taiwan reported that Chinese coast guard and research ships appeared near key South China Sea islands. Beijing sent its largest patrol ship east of Taiwan as a show of force.

The increased military activity came in direct response to diplomatic discussions between Tokyo and Manila. Taiwan's coast guard said it expelled Chinese ships from restricted waters. The patrols represent China's objection to what it views as regional cooperation aimed at countering its influence in the South China Sea and around Taiwan.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping to visit North Korea
cards.teaser: China's leader is making a rare trip to North Korea for talks with Kim Jong Un.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week in his first visit since 2019. Both countries announced the trip on Friday, a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility to produce nuclear fuel.

The visit marks a rare high-level diplomatic engagement between Beijing and Pyongyang. China and North Korea have maintained their longstanding alliance, though such visits between the countries' leaders have been infrequent in recent years.

cards.headline: Trump administration uses compliance schemes to control higher education
cards.teaser: The White House is exercising substantial influence over colleges through reporting requirements that avoid legislative approval.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is using compliance and reporting schemes to exercise substantial control over college operations without securing legislative approval or generating public debate. These mechanisms allow the White House to influence how colleges and universities govern themselves, whom they admit and hire, what they teach, the research they conduct, and how they define educational quality.

These compliance requirements tend to fly below the radar but collectively have an immense impact on higher education institutions. The approach allows the administration to shape university policies and practices through administrative pressure rather than through Congress or public policy debates.

cards.headline: Intoxicating hemp industry pushes Congress for relief as ban approaches
cards.teaser: The industry has until November to convince lawmakers to delay or stop a ban on hemp-derived intoxicants.
cards.body:
The intoxicating hemp industry and its supporters are racing against time to convince Congress to block or delay a ban on their products scheduled for November. Sen. Mitch McConnell championed the prohibition, which was included in last fall's government funding legislation.

While bipartisan support exists for disrupting the ban, lawmakers have yet to take concrete action. The industry faces a shrinking window to secure legislative intervention before the market-altering prohibition takes effect.

cards.headline: Zelensky condemns drone strike near Chornobyl nuclear plant
cards.teaser: Ukrainian officials said a Russian drone hit a storage facility for spent nuclear fuel.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned a Russian drone strike near the Chornobyl nuclear plant as deliberate and "extremely vile." A Shahed drone damaged a building used to store spent nuclear fuel at the site, according to Ukrainian officials.

The reception building of the spent fuel storage facility was empty of containers at the time of the attack. The strike appeared to be a direct message from Moscow amid an intensifying campaign of long-range aerial strikes targeting high-profile locations on both sides. The attack occurred as Zelensky prepared for talks in London.

hero.headline: Gunman kills one, wounds five in shooting in central Israel
hero.body:
Shooting at Louisiana Mardi Gras Parade Wounds Five, Including Child

A shooting during a Mardi Gras parade in Clinton, Louisiana on Saturday left five people wounded, including a six-year-old child, authorities said. The incident occurred shortly after the midday start of the Mardi Gras in the Country parade.

East Feliciana Sheriff Jeff Travis told reporters that three people carrying firearms were taken into custody at the scene, though investigators had not yet determined whether they were involved in the shooting. Louisiana State Police took over the investigation following the incident.

Chief Criminal Deputy Bill Cox from the sheriff's office said all five victims were expected to survive, though specific details about their conditions were not immediately released. The sheriff's office appealed to the public for assistance, asking anyone who photographed or recorded the shooting or nearby areas to share that material with investigators.

Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry responded to the shooting on social media, describing it as "absolutely horrific and unacceptable" and calling for prayers for the victims.

Clinton, a town of approximately 1,300 people located in the metropolitan area surrounding Baton Rouge, Louisiana's capital, has now been the site of a significant shooting incident during what should have been a community celebration.

The shooting comes as gun violence continues at high rates across the United States. According to the nonpartisan Gun Violence Archive, at least 24 mass shootings had occurred in the country by the time of the Louisiana incident. The archive defines a mass shooting as an incident in which four or more victims are wounded or killed.

The persistent occurrence of mass shootings in America has prompted calls from many quarters for Congress to implement stricter gun control measures. However, lawmakers have historically shown reluctance or inability to pass meaningful legislation addressing the issue, despite ongoing public pressure and repeated incidents of gun violence.

The investigation into the Clinton parade shooting is ongoing as authorities work to determine the circumstances of the incident and establish whether the three people taken into custody had any involvement in the violence that unfolded during the community event.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping to visit North Korea
cards.teaser: China's leader is making a rare trip to North Korea for talks with Kim Jong Un.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week in his first visit since 2019. Both countries announced the trip on Friday, a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility to produce nuclear fuel.

The visit marks a rare high-level diplomatic engagement between Beijing and Pyongyang. China and North Korea have maintained their longstanding alliance, though such visits between the countries' leaders have been infrequent in recent years.

cards.headline: Peru holds presidential runoff between left and right candidates
cards.teaser: Voters face a choice between a moderated leftist and a right-wing candidate representing an autocrat's legacy.
cards.body:
Peruvians are voting in a runoff election between Keiko Fujimori, daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, and leftist congressman Roberto Sánchez. Fujimori won 17 percent in the first round while Sánchez secured 12 percent, positioning them for a polarized left-right contest that mirrors Peru's 2021 election.

The race unfolds against a backdrop of rising crime, political instability, and widespread corruption scandals. Peru has had nine presidents in a decade, leaving many voters exhausted and searching for stability. Security and inequality have become dominant concerns as voters decide between the two candidates.

cards.headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes Europe on migration in D-Day speech
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth used an 82nd anniversary speech in Normandy to attack European migration policy.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth drew widespread criticism after linking immigration to D-Day during a speech in Normandy marking the 82nd anniversary of the allied landings. Speaking in northwestern France, Hegseth described Europe as facing a different "invasion" of its shores, using the occasion to attack European immigration policies.

Historians and rights campaigners condemned the remarks as "grotesque stupidity," accusing Hegseth of desecrating the memory of soldiers who died liberating Nazi-occupied Europe. Residents of a nearby French village also said he was not welcome for the commemoration event.

cards.headline: China increases patrols near Taiwan after Japan-Philippines talks
cards.teaser: Beijing deployed coast guard and research ships near key South China Sea islands in protest.
cards.body:
China escalated naval patrols near Taiwan following talks between Japan and the Philippines. Taiwan reported that Chinese coast guard and research ships appeared near key South China Sea islands. Beijing sent its largest patrol ship east of Taiwan as a show of force.

The increased military activity came in direct response to diplomatic discussions between Tokyo and Manila. Taiwan's coast guard said it expelled Chinese ships from restricted waters. The patrols represent China's objection to what it views as regional cooperation aimed at countering its influence in the South China Sea and around Taiwan.

cards.headline: Pope draws over one million people to Mass in Madrid
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV held an open-air Mass in Spain's capital during his first papal visit in 15 years.
cards.body:
More than one million people gathered near Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles for an outdoor Mass led by Pope Leo. As he arrived in his white popemobile, crowds waved flags, shouted "Long live the pope," and tossed flower petals in celebration.

The event marked the pope's first visit to an EU country outside Italy. During his week-long visit to Spain, the pontiff urged world leaders to stop dividing electorates and to respect every human being.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drone attacks hit St. Petersburg during economic forum
cards.teaser: Russia's flagship economic event was disrupted by drone strikes on the city.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck St. Petersburg while Russia's major economic forum was underway in the city. The attacks disrupted what was meant to be a flagship showcase event for President Putin, with the BBC's Russia editor witnessing the disruptions firsthand.

The timing of the strikes appeared intended to undermine the high-profile international gathering and demonstrate Ukraine's capacity to reach deep into Russian territory. The incident highlighted security challenges for Russian air defenses in protecting even symbolically important cities.

hero.headline: Gunfire wounds at least 12 near Ohio street festival
hero.body:
At least 12 people were wounded after gunfire erupted near a busy street festival in Toledo, Ohio. The shooting occurred near the Old West End Festival, sending some attendees scrambling for cover while others rushed to help the injured. Two victims sustained critical injuries. Police are still searching for multiple suspects.

The violence unfolded in a crowded area as the festival was underway. Witnesses reported hearing gunshots that prompted immediate panic among festivalgoers. Emergency responders arrived to treat the wounded at the scene before transporting them to local hospitals. The festival was taking place on a busy street when the attack occurred.

Authorities have not apprehended any suspects and are conducting an active manhunt. Police described the level of violence as exceptional for the area. Local leaders addressed the shooting in public statements, though law enforcement has not released descriptions of the suspects or disclosed a possible motive for the attack.

The shooting adds to a series of public gatherings across the country that have been disrupted by gun violence. Toledo police are asking anyone with information about the incident to come forward. The investigation continues as authorities work to identify and locate those responsible.

The Old West End Festival typically draws large crowds to the historic neighborhood. The event was disrupted as police secured the area and began their investigation. Families and festival attendees who had gathered for the community event were left shaken by the sudden outbreak of violence in what is normally a festive atmosphere.

cards.headline: Police track activity critical of AI in Philadelphia
cards.teaser: Philadelphia police acknowledged monitoring First Amendment activity that criticizes artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Philadelphia police have admitted to tracking First Amendment activity that is critical of artificial intelligence technology. The monitoring comes as federal agencies including the FBI and Department of Homeland Security track what they characterize as anti-tech extremism amid growing public backlash against the rapid expansion of AI.

The surveillance of speech related to AI has raised concerns about thought policing and the boundaries of legitimate protest. The tracking occurs as technology companies accelerate AI development and deployment, which has sparked resistance from some segments of the American public who view the pace of technological change as threatening.

cards.headline: Pope draws one million to Madrid procession
cards.teaser: Pope Leo's visit to Spain attracted massive crowds for a flower-carpeted procession through the capital.
cards.body:
More than one million people gathered in Madrid's streets near Plaza de Cibeles to attend an outdoor Mass led by Pope Leo. Crowds pressed along barriers, waving flags and shouting "Long live the pope" as the pontiff arrived in his white popemobile. Some attendees tossed flower petals to welcome him.

This marks Pope Leo's first visit to Spain in 15 years and his first trip to an EU country outside Italy. During the Mass, the pope urged world leaders to stop dividing electorates and to respect every human being. The event is expected to be the largest gathering of his week-long visit to Spain.

cards.headline: Five arrested over protests following fatal stabbing in Southampton
cards.teaser: A 16-year-old girl was among five people arrested after disorder erupted at protests in Southampton.
cards.body:
Five people were arrested during disorder that broke out at protests in Southampton on Tuesday. A 16-year-old girl was among those taken into custody near the location where 18-year-old Henry Nowak was fatally stabbed.

Three individuals have been charged in connection with the unrest that erupted during the demonstrations.

cards.headline: UK foreign secretary confronts Vance over migration comments
cards.teaser: David Lammy told the vice president his remarks linking a fatal stabbing to migration were wrong.
cards.body:
British Foreign Secretary David Lammy confronted Vice President JD Vance over comments linking an 18-year-old's death to migration. Vance had blamed Henry Nowak's fatal stabbing on what he described as a "mass invasion of migrants." Lammy told Vance his characterization was wrong, stating the death has nothing to do with mass migration.

The disagreement reflects broader tensions between US and UK officials over how they frame issues of crime and immigration. The exchange comes as US Defense Secretary Hegseth has also made similar comparisons, using "invasion" language to describe migration to Europe during a speech in Normandy.

cards.headline: Defense secretary addresses migration in D-Day anniversary speech
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth used a Normandy speech to criticize European migration policy, describing beach invasions.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered a speech in Normandy on the 82nd anniversary of D-Day, using the World War II commemoration to criticize European migration policies. Speaking at the site where Allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe, Hegseth drew comparisons between migration and beach invasions.

The remarks directly addressed Europe's approach to migration policy during the anniversary event.

cards.headline: Zelensky condemns drone strike near Chornobyl nuclear plant
cards.teaser: Ukrainian officials said a Russian drone hit a storage facility for spent nuclear fuel.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned a Russian drone strike near the Chornobyl nuclear plant as deliberate and "extremely vile." A Shahed drone damaged a building used to store spent nuclear fuel at the site, according to Ukrainian officials.

The reception building of the spent fuel storage facility was empty of containers at the time of the attack. The strike appeared to be a direct message from Moscow amid an intensifying campaign of long-range aerial strikes targeting high-profile locations on both sides. The attack occurred as Zelensky prepared for talks in London.

cards.headline: Paramount Open to Selling Kids Channels in Warner Bros. Deal
cards.teaser: Paramount has indicated willingness to divest children's programming channels to address European Union regulatory concerns over its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.
cards.body:
Paramount is prepared to sell its kids channels to satisfy European Union regulators reviewing the company's proposed $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. The concession comes as antitrust authorities examine the combined entity's market power across entertainment sectors.

The merger has drawn opposition from industry workers, who held a town hall expressing concerns about job losses and industry consolidation. Multiple U.S. states have announced plans to file lawsuits to block the deal. A Paramount lawyer has responded to merger opponents, claiming some hold antisemitic views, adding controversy to an already contested corporate combination.

cards.headline: CaaStle CEO Remained in Charge After Fraud Confession
cards.teaser: The board of fashion tech startup CaaStle allowed CEO Christine Hunsicker to stay in her role after she confessed to defrauding the company.
cards.body:
Christine Hunsicker admitted to defrauding CaaStle, the fashion tech startup she led as chief executive, but the company's board permitted her to continue running the organization. The final months of the company's operations included fake audits and stock buybacks as part of a damage control effort.

Hunsicker herself led the damage control strategy despite being the person who had committed the fraud. The unusual arrangement raises questions about corporate governance practices at the startup, which operated a clothing rental and subscription service for retailers.

cards.headline: Retail Investors Seek Access to SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: Individual investors are exploring ways to purchase shares in SpaceX as the company prepares for a public offering valued at $1.8 trillion.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's SpaceX is moving toward an initial public offering, prompting retail investors to investigate how they can participate in the stock sale. The company carries a valuation of $1.8 trillion, making it one of the largest IPOs in history.

Financial advisors are counseling investors to wait for an initial price decline before purchasing shares. Wall Street analysts are debating the investment merits of the space company, with some noting that the massive IPO will introduce unusual dynamics to the market for space-related stocks.

cards.headline: Broadcom Stock Falls Despite Earnings Beat
cards.teaser: Broadcom shares declined after the company reported earnings, with analysts describing conservative guidance as a reality check on artificial intelligence investment momentum.
cards.body:
Bank of America has adjusted its price target for Broadcom following the chip company's latest earnings report. The stock fell despite beating earnings expectations, with Wall Street interpreting the results as a pause in the artificial intelligence trade that has driven tech valuations higher.

Analysts characterized the market reaction as a splash of cold water on AI enthusiasm, though some believe the decline represents an overreaction to conservative forward guidance. Morningstar and other research firms are examining whether Broadcom's premium valuation remains justified given the company's growth outlook.

cards.headline: WWE Shareholder Lawsuit Trial Canceled
cards.teaser: A trial related to WWE's merger has been removed from the court calendar, sparing Vince McMahon from immediate testimony.
cards.body:
The trial for a shareholder lawsuit related to WWE's merger has been canceled and taken off the Delaware court schedule. The case had been set to proceed with testimony from Vince McMahon and other company executives.

The abrupt cancellation removes legal pressure from WWE leadership in the short term.

cards.headline: Debt Collectors Face Abuse as More Americans Fall Behind on Bills
cards.teaser: Workers in the debt collection industry report enduring verbal abuse and threats of violence as rising numbers of Americans take on debt and miss payments.
cards.body:
Debt collection workers are experiencing increased hostility from callers as more Americans accumulate debt and fall behind on bill payments. Collectors report regular verbal abuse and threats of violence during calls to recover overdue payments.

The rising confrontations reflect broader economic stress as household debt levels climb. Collection workers describe the emotional toll of their jobs, which require them to pursue payment from people experiencing financial hardship while absorbing the anger and frustration those situations generate.

hero.headline: School shooting survivor sues AI gun detection company after weapon went undetected
hero.body:
A survivor of a school shooting has filed a lawsuit against an artificial intelligence gun detection firm after the company's system failed to identify a weapon before the attack occurred. The legal action raises questions about the reliability standards required for AI security systems deployed in schools and other public spaces.

The lawsuit centers on the performance of an AI-based weapon detection system that was in place at the school when the shooting happened. According to the complaint, the technology failed to alert authorities to the presence of a firearm, allowing the weapon to enter the facility undetected. The survivor argues that the company's system did not perform as advertised, potentially contributing to the harm that followed.

The case highlights broader debates about the deployment of artificial intelligence in security applications. As schools and other institutions increasingly turn to automated detection systems to enhance safety, questions have emerged about how accurate these technologies need to be before they can be relied upon for life-or-death situations. The lawsuit may force courts to establish clearer standards for what constitutes acceptable performance in AI security systems.

Gun detection technology using artificial intelligence has been marketed as a way to identify weapons quickly without the invasiveness of metal detectors or manual searches. These systems typically analyze video feeds or other sensor data to spot firearms. Proponents argue that AI can process information faster than human security personnel, potentially stopping threats before they escalate. Critics counter that the technology remains imperfect and that over-reliance on automated systems can create a false sense of security.

The outcome of the lawsuit could have significant implications for the AI security industry. If courts determine that the company's system fell short of reasonable standards, it may establish legal precedent affecting how such technologies are tested, marketed, and deployed. Schools and other organizations using similar systems may also face pressure to re-evaluate their security protocols and the role that AI plays in protecting students and staff.

cards.headline: Bumblebees demonstrate problem-solving abilities comparable to larger-brained animals
cards.teaser: Research shows bumblebees can solve complex problems spontaneously, challenging assumptions about the relationship between brain size and intelligence.
cards.body:
Scientists have found that bumblebees can solve problems with a level of sophistication previously associated only with animals possessing much larger brains, such as chimpanzees and elephants. The research challenges long-held assumptions that complex cognitive abilities require substantial neural architecture.

The study demonstrated that bumblebees displayed spontaneous problem-solving skills, tackling tasks without prior training. Researchers observed the insects using tool-like behaviors to overcome obstacles and achieve goals. The findings suggest that intelligence and problem-solving capacity may not depend solely on brain size, but rather on how neural networks are organized and utilized.

cards.headline: Xbox Games Showcase 2026 features first presentation by new head Asha Sharma
cards.teaser: Microsoft held its annual Xbox Games Showcase with Asha Sharma presenting for the first time as the division's new leader.
cards.body:
Microsoft presented its Xbox Games Showcase 2026, marking the first time Asha Sharma led the event in her new role. The showcase included announcements and updates on upcoming games for the Xbox platform. The event also featured a dedicated segment on Gears of War: E-Day.

The presentation covered multiple titles including Fable and Project Helix, among others. The showcase represents what Microsoft describes as the next era for Xbox. Multiple gaming outlets provided live coverage of the announcements as they were revealed during the stream.

cards.headline: Scientists removed from diabetes conference after distributing journal articles
cards.teaser: Medical researchers including a journal editor and former association president were ejected from a diabetes conference for handing out reprints.
cards.body:
Several prominent diabetes researchers, including Steven Kahn (editor-in-chief of an American Diabetes Association journal) and Desmond Schatz (a former ADA president), were ejected from a diabetes conference for distributing reprints of journal articles. The scientists were escorted from the venue during the event.

The incident has drawn attention within the diabetes research community, raising questions about the conference's policies on materials distribution and the circumstances that led to the removal of these established figures in the field.

cards.headline: Game director Hideo Kojima says he has no interest in using AI for creative work
cards.teaser: The prominent video game creator stated he does not believe he will see artificial intelligence create true art during his lifetime.
cards.body:
Video game director Hideo Kojima has stated he is not interested in using artificial intelligence in his creative work. The developer behind the Metal Gear and Death Stranding franchises expressed skepticism about AI's artistic capabilities.

While Kojima acknowledged that AI might eventually become capable of creating art, he does not believe this will happen during his lifetime. His position reflects broader debates within creative industries about artificial intelligence's role in producing original artistic works.

cards.headline: Vampire Survivors announces Nintendo Switch 2 version and new expansion
cards.teaser: The indie game will receive a port for Nintendo's next console along with new downloadable content and a title update.
cards.body:
Developer Poncle announced that Vampire Survivors will be released for the Nintendo Switch 2, the upcoming successor to Nintendo's current console. The company also revealed a new expansion titled Legacy Of The Bloodmoon and other updates for the game.

Alongside the Switch 2 announcement, Poncle disclosed plans to establish a new studio in Japan. The Japanese studio will be led by Sawaki Takeyasu, known for his work on the game El Shaddai. The announcements were made during a gaming showcase event.

cards.headline: Remastered version of Godzilla fighting game coming to PlayStation 5 in November
cards.teaser: A remaster of the 2002 game Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee will launch on current-generation consoles later this year.
cards.body:
A remastered version of Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, originally released in 2002, will debut on PlayStation 5 this November. The kaiju fighting game is being brought back with updated graphics and features for modern gaming systems.

The remaster will also be available on Nintendo Switch 2, according to reports. The original game allowed players to control various giant monsters in arena battles. The updated version aims to introduce the title to a new generation of players while appealing to fans of the original release.

hero.headline: Zverev and Cobolli compete in French Open final
hero.body:
Alexander Zverev and Flavio Cobolli faced off in the French Open men's singles final at Roland-Garros, with both players seeking their first Grand Slam title. The match represented a significant moment for each competitor on one of tennis's biggest stages.

Zverev, a veteran on the professional tour, arrived at the final after multiple previous attempts at major championships. He lost the 2020 US Open final to Dominic Thiem from two sets up and fell to Carlos Alcaraz in the 2024 French Open final. More recently, he lost to Jannik Sinner in the 2025 Australian Open final. This fortnight presented what observers described as the opportunity of a lifetime, with both Alcaraz sidelined by injury and Sinner eliminated by illness.

The German player's path to the Roland-Garros final carried particular significance: he became the first player since Mats Wilander in 1988 whose opponents in the round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals and final had never reached those stages before. Despite not playing at his absolute best, Zverev proved sufficiently strong for every opponent he faced.

Cobolli, the Italian competitor, arrived at his first Grand Slam final in what represented a breakthrough moment in his professional career. The 26-year-old had developed into a top-10 talent, displaying a tremendous forehand, excellent returning ability and exceptional movement around the court. Observers noted he was perhaps the quickest player on tour and competed with intensity characteristic of elite competitors.

According to Coach Calv Betton, a respected analyst, "Cobolli is a quality player with no stand out weaknesses. He can live with Zverev off the ground and even beat him." However, Betton also noted that modern men's tennis operates under constraints: "The men's game now they all play the same. There isn't much tactically. They're all baseline ball strikers and it's just whoever hits it better."

Tactically, some analysts suggested Cobolli's best approach involved keeping Zverev moving rather than simply hitting winners. This strategy could include drop-shots to exploit Cobolli's net skills, angled balls breaking the sidelines and deep balls toward corners. Such tactics aimed to prevent Zverev from planting his feet and settling into extended baseline exchanges.

While many observers considered the final a potential mismatch favoring Zverev, the reality proved more nuanced. Zverev possessed weaknesses in his forehand and volleying that Cobolli could potentially exploit. The question remained whether the pressure of finally reaching a Grand Slam final would inspire Zverev or paralyze his performance when he needed it most.

For both players, this match offered the opportunity to secure a career-defining victory and join the ranks of Grand Slam champions, though the paths they traveled to reach this stage differed considerably in experience and circumstances.

cards.headline: England defeats New Zealand by 115 runs in opening Test
cards.teaser: England secured victory in the first Test against New Zealand at Lord's, beginning their post-Ashes rebuild with a win on the fourth day.
cards.body:
England completed a 115-run victory over New Zealand in the opening Test at Lord's, wrapping up the match in less than a session on the fourth day. The win marked the beginning of England's rebuild following their recent Ashes campaign.

Gus Atkinson was instrumental in securing the result, claiming additional wickets in New Zealand's second innings. Despite resistance from Devon Conway and Glenn Phillips, England's bowling attack proved too strong as the visitors fell short in their chase.

cards.headline: Golden Knights beat Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime after blowing four-goal lead
cards.teaser: Vegas defeated Carolina in Game 3 of their playoff series, winning in the second overtime period despite surrendering a four-goal advantage.
cards.body:
Shea Theodore scored at 5:38 of the second overtime period to lift the Vegas Golden Knights past the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final. The goal, which deflected off goalie Brandon Bussi's skate, gave Vegas a 2-1 series lead and prevented what would have been a devastating collapse.

The Golden Knights had built a commanding four-goal advantage before the Hurricanes staged a remarkable comeback to force overtime. Mitch Marner recorded the fastest hat trick in Stanley Cup Final history during the contest, adding to Vegas's initial dominance before Carolina's dramatic rally.

cards.headline: Nelly Korda shares lead at US Women's Open as Charley Hull moves into contention
cards.teaser: Korda shot a four-under 67 to move into a tie for the lead after the third round, while England's Hull posted a 65 to storm up the leaderboard.
cards.body:
Nelly Kord moved into a share of the lead after the third round of the US Women's Open, firing a four-under par 67 to position herself at the top heading into the final day.

England's Charley Hull surged into contention with a strong showing of her own, carding a 65 in the third round to climb the leaderboard as the championship approaches its conclusion.

cards.headline: Messi rested as teams complete World Cup warm-up matches
cards.teaser: Argentina sat Lionel Messi for their friendly against Honduras, while Brazil, Germany, Belgium and Portugal each won pre-World Cup games.
cards.body:
Argentina rested Lionel Messi in their friendly against Honduras, giving the veteran forward extra recovery time before the World Cup. The decision came as part of Argentina's final preparations for the tournament.

Several top nations secured victories in their warm-up matches. England defeated New Zealand 1-0 with a goal from Harry Kane, while Scotland dominated Bolivia in their final tune-up before their first World Cup appearance in 28 years. Brazil, Germany, Belgium and Portugal also won their respective warm-up fixtures as teams finalized their preparations ahead of the competition.

cards.headline: Germany defeats USA 2-1 in World Cup send-off match
cards.teaser: Germany beat the United States in a pre-World Cup friendly, though injuries to players cast a shadow over the result for both teams.
cards.body:
Germany won their World Cup warm-up match against the United States 2-1, giving both teams a final chance to prepare before the tournament. The friendly allowed coaches to assess their squads in competitive action.

The match took a toll on both teams, with injuries sustained during play raising concerns as the World Cup approaches. Such physical demands in pre-tournament friendlies can impact squad availability in the critical days before competition begins.

cards.headline: Gabriel Bonfim defeats Belal Muhammad at UFC Fight Night
cards.teaser: Bonfim dominated Muhammad in the main event at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
Gabriel Bonfim secured a dominant victory over Belal Muhammad in the main event of UFC Fight Night. The Brazilian fighter controlled the bout to earn the win at the Las Vegas venue.

The fight card featured preliminary bouts leading up to the main event. Bonfim's performance against Muhammad highlighted the evening's competition at UFC Vegas 118.

hero.headline: Scott Pelley Calls for Removal of CBS News Chief Bari Weiss
hero.body:
Former 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley has publicly called for the removal of Bari Weiss as head of the CBS News division following his firing from the long-running news program. Pelley's departure came after an explosive confrontation with Nick Bilton, the show's newly appointed executive producer.

The conflict escalated during a heated Monday morning meeting where Pelley criticized Weiss's leadership. According to reports, Pelley stated that Weiss "does not love this place" and suggested she "was brought in to kill it." He also told colleagues that she was "murdering 60 Minutes."

CBS News management had terminated the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi, without providing specific reasons for their dismissals. Executives attempted to meet with Pelley following these terminations, but he initially declined. When he finally met with Weiss and other executives on Tuesday, they conveyed that his conduct in the previous day's meeting was inappropriate.

Bilton informed Pelley by message on Tuesday evening that he had been "terminated for cause effective immediately." In his communication, Bilton referenced Pelley's behavior, stating that "you hijacked my first meeting with staff to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt."

Pelley, who joined CBS News in 1989 and had worked at 60 Minutes since 2004, later issued a public statement accusing the network's new executives of silencing employees. He claimed they instructed him "to inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. In his statement shared on social media, Pelley emphasized that 60 Minutes has remained the top-rated program in America "because our beloved audience finds integrity, quality, and humanity in our stories."

Weiss, a former New York Times opinion editor and founder of the independent news site The Free Press, was appointed as editor-in-chief in October as part of a restructuring under parent company Paramount Skydance. Her appointment marked a departure from traditional network news leadership, with her background primarily in print and digital media rather than television production.

With Pelley's departure and Anderson Cooper's earlier announcement that he would be leaving the program, 60 Minutes is left with only three full-time correspondents: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and L Jon Wertheim. CBS News journalist and former evening news anchor Norah O'Donnell contributes to the show.

The situation represents one of the most visible leadership conflicts in recent CBS News history, with veteran journalists openly challenging executive decisions in major publications. Weiss has not publicly responded to Pelley's comments or accusations.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Premieres Duet With The Cure's Robert Smith at Primavera Sound
cards.teaser: The pop star revealed an unexpected collaboration with the rock legend by debuting a new song from her upcoming album.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo brought Robert Smith of The Cure onstage at Primavera Sound festival to perform their duet, a previously secret track titled What's Wrong With Me. The surprise performance revealed one of the most unexpected collaborations on Rodrigo's forthcoming album, which releases in less than a week.

The pairing marks an unusual cross-generational partnership between the 23-year-old pop star and the 67-year-old alternative rock icon. Rodrigo's team had kept the collaboration under wraps until the festival premiere, making it one of the most closely guarded secrets in pop music this year.

cards.headline: Tribeca Festival Condemns Jokes About Palestinian Rape Made on Red Carpet
cards.teaser: The film festival issued a statement calling remarks by comedian Elon Gold and influencer Lizzy Savetsky offensive and unacceptable.
cards.body:
The Tribeca Festival publicly condemned jokes about Palestinian rape made on the red carpet of The Wedding Entertainer by comedian Elon Gold and influencer Lizzy Savetsky. The comments were captured on video and quickly circulated across social media, prompting swift backlash.

In a statement, the festival called the remarks offensive and unacceptable, emphasizing that human suffering should never be mocked. The incident occurred at the premiere of The Wedding Entertainer, also known as The Tale of Moishe Badhan, and drew significant attention away from the film itself.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Opens First Tour in Six Years in Oakland
cards.teaser: The pop star performed the opening night of her Eternal Sunshine tour after more than six years away from concert stages.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande returned to touring with the opening night of her Eternal Sunshine tour at Oakland Arena on Saturday. The show marked her first concert tour in six and a half years, featuring performances across her musical catalog.

The tour takes its name from Grande's recent album and is expected to continue through 2026, signaling a major comeback to live performance for the pop star.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Cancels Second Pittsburgh Concert Due to Weather
cards.teaser: The country star called off his Acrisure Stadium show citing severe weather conditions and safety concerns.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen canceled his second scheduled concert at Pittsburgh's Acrisure Stadium due to severe weather conditions. The postponement affected thousands of fans who had tickets for the second of two planned performances in the city.

Wallen publicly addressed the cancellation, apparently responding to fan concerns about the decision.

cards.headline: Charlie Puth Cancels Orlando Show Due to Illness
cards.teaser: The singer announced on Instagram that he must cancel his performance after being sick for several days.
cards.body:
Charlie Puth announced on Instagram Story that he was forced to cancel his Saturday show in Orlando, Florida due to illness. The singer expressed his devastation over the decision, stating he was heartbroken about having to pull out of the performance.

Puth had been dealing with sickness for several days and was advised by medical professionals to rest rather than perform, which could have worsened his condition.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Thanks Supporters After 60 Minutes Firing
cards.teaser: The veteran journalist posted on Instagram expressing gratitude for messages he received following his dismissal from the CBS program.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley posted a message on Instagram thanking supporters after his firing from 60 Minutes. The veteran correspondent stated that supporters are the wind in his sails following an outpouring of messages.

In a public statement, Pelley accused CBS News executives of instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He emphasized that 60 Minutes built its decades-long success as America's top program through integrity, quality, and humanity. Pelley's dismissal followed a clash with the network's new management, sparking criticism from colleagues and the daughter of late correspondent Morley Safer, who questioned the direction of the program under current CBS News leadership.

hero.headline: White House AI policy adviser to step down at end of month
hero.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a key figure in developing the Trump administration's AI strategy, confirmed he will leave his position.
hero.body:
Sriram Krishnan, a tech investor serving as a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, has confirmed his departure at the end of this month.

Krishnan held a central role in the Trump administration's AI initiatives, helping to shape strategic plans aligned with the president's artificial intelligence objectives. His exit marks the loss of a key figure from the White House team focused on AI policy during a period when the technology continues to transform industries and raise important questions about regulation and infrastructure needs.

cards.headline: Trump administration delays major drone deal with Ukraine
cards.teaser: The White House has not signed an agreement with Ukraine on drone production despite months of talks and Ukrainian requests.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's hesitation to sign a major drone deal with Ukraine is slowing U.S. military progress in an area where it already lags. Talks between the two nations have stretched back to at least September, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urging Washington to finalize the agreement.

The delay is affecting the U.S. military's ability to advance its drone capabilities. The prolonged negotiations have left experts questioning why the administration has not moved forward on a deal that Ukrainian leadership considers important for both countries' defense capabilities.

cards.headline: Intoxicating hemp industry pushes Congress for relief as ban approaches
cards.teaser: The industry has until November to convince lawmakers to delay or stop a ban on hemp-derived intoxicants.
cards.body:
The intoxicating hemp industry and its supporters are racing against time to convince Congress to block or delay a ban on their products scheduled for November. Sen. Mitch McConnell championed the prohibition, which was included in last fall's government funding legislation.

While bipartisan support exists for disrupting the ban, lawmakers have yet to take concrete action. The industry faces a shrinking window to secure legislative intervention before the market-altering prohibition takes effect.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in the general election.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Her victory positions her for a general election race where she could make history.

If Haaland wins in November, she would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history. The former Cabinet official now faces the task of building a coalition for the general election in a state that has trended Democratic in recent cycles.

cards.headline: Democrats see opportunity in Iowa Senate race after Turek primary win
cards.teaser: State Rep. Josh Turek's nomination gives Democrats renewed hope in a state where they have struggled to compete.
cards.body:
Democrats are viewing Iowa's U.S. Senate race with renewed optimism after state Rep. Josh Turek secured the party's nomination. Party officials consider it their best chance to compete for the seat in years.

Turek, a 47-year-old two-time Paralympic gold medalist with a history of winning in conservative areas, defeated state Sen. Zach Wahls, 34, in the primary. Democrats believe Turek's background and proven ability to win over Republican-leaning voters gives them a credible candidate in a state that has moved away from the party in recent election cycles.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Early results show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra ahead in the race to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton is leading the Republican primary while Xavier Becerra has advanced to the general election on the Democratic side in California's gubernatorial race. Becerra's strong finish marks a remarkable turnaround after his campaign polled at just 3% in late March.

If elected, Becerra would make history as California's first Latino governor since 1875. California's top-two primary system means the general election could feature two candidates from the same party depending on who finishes second in their respective primaries.

cards.headline: New York City Mayor Mamdani says Democrats lost focus on working people
cards.teaser: The mayor argued the party has strayed from economic issues important to working-class Americans.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Democrats have lost sight of the important economic issues facing working-class Americans as the party works to rebuild after losing the 2024 presidential election. Mamdani made the comments in an interview about the party's future direction.

Mamdani stated that the party as a whole has lost its focus on working people. His critique adds to ongoing discussions within the Democratic Party about how to regain support from voters who have drifted away over concerns about economic policy and priorities.
